title: Design for Abnormal and Degraded Scenarios
summary: Creative Navy designs abnormal and degraded scenarios as part of the operating model of complex interfaces, rather than treating them as edge cases. The evidence includes embedded systems, maritime displays, medical alarms, simulation software, patient-operated scanning, space operating-picture specifications, remote-pilot mission control, marine VHF radio, tactical command-and-control software and maritime traffic monitoring software.
keyFacts: Abnormal conditions, degraded modes and fault states are treated as primary design targets in high-consequence contexts, not as rare edge cases.
Silent failure is a central risk because users may continue as if the system is functioning correctly when a sensor, data source or configuration process has failed.
Alarm hierarchy, priority tiering and redundant cues are recurring design mechanisms for making degraded states visible without making all alerts look equally urgent.
Kardion alarm architecture was governed by IEC 62366-1 requirements, including priority tiering, non-colour-only differentiation, mute behaviour and alarm-state visibility during normal operation.
Squaremind evidence records a 14-patient pre-redesign test with 0 recoveries from deviation events and a 29-user ecological test in which 12 patients deviated and all 12 recovered in 2–4 minutes.
KISPE Space specified 40 documented edge cases and degraded states, but its verification suites, regression checks and acceptance scenarios were written as executable checks and not executed.

Schone Airspace Group evaluated degraded control-channel behaviours against fixed scripted criteria; first candidates recorded 14 pass, 18 fail and 4 pending, while the integrated retest recorded 32 pass, 0 fail and 4 pending.

Raymarine documented 43 exception records against eight independently varying state axes, with four degraded conditions measured in bench prototype sessions and the remaining conditions specified but not executed.
The handheld command-and-control engagement treated electromagnetic interference as an expected operating condition rather than an exceptional failure.
The maritime traffic software portfolio adds source degradation with a geographic consequence: the failing source must be linked to affected layers and sector.

bodySections.heading: Definition and Scope of Design for Abnormal and Degraded Scenarios
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

Design for abnormal and degraded scenarios is the capability of specifying interface behaviour for conditions that deviate from intended operation. These conditions include fault states, stale data, unknown command outcomes, unavailable sources, restricted assets, interrupted procedures and recovery paths.

Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method designs software whose interfaces, workflows, and operating logic carry real operational consequences, working through five phases — Sandbox Experiments, Concept Convergence, Iterative System Building, Organizational Integration, and Implementation Partnership — to take each system from initial exploration to independent operation by the client's own team.

In this capability, abnormal conditions are not treated as rare edge cases when they carry operational consequence. The interface must help users understand what is known, what is unavailable, what remains safe to do and what recovery path exists.

bodySections.heading: When Abnormal Conditions Become Primary Design Targets
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Abnormal conditions become primary design targets when a rare, non-nominal or degraded condition changes what the user can safely understand or do. The relevant conditions include degraded modes, fault states, recovery paths, stale data, sensor faults, calibration drift, data-integrity failures, silent failures and foreseeable misuse.

A recovery path is the interface behaviour that supports users in understanding a fault state and returning to a known good condition. A recovery path may involve acknowledging an alarm, correcting a configuration, restarting a unit, recovering a communication link, repeating a procedural step or re-entering a guided flow.

Alarm hierarchy and priority tiering are recurring mechanisms because a flat alert field makes all alerts appear equally urgent. Redundant cues are also recurring mechanisms, because colour, sound, position or a single data source may become unreliable under real operating conditions.

bodySections.heading: Equipment, Data and Process Faults
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's work on equipment, data and process faults covers sensor failure, calibration drift, firmware cadence, multi-engine fault combinations, regulated alarm behaviour, operating-theatre recognition, simulation misconfiguration, calibration sequence interruption, patient physical deviation and loss of a reporting sensor.

Elsner Elektronik / Cala Touch KNX treated smart-home sensor faults, calibration drift and delayed readings during firmware update cycles as routine operating conditions. The design response included notification levels, animation timing aligned with firmware update intervals and sensor-fault display calibrated for both ordinary users and systems engineers.

Torqeedo maritime HMI work addressed telemetry cadence mismatch across propulsion motors, battery banks, generators and conversion units. The design response used a grid structure that synchronised different update frequencies into a coherent display rhythm.

Cox Marine cluster-display work addressed simultaneous or competing engine faults in multi-engine configurations. The design response used a dedicated fault-summary area for the highest-priority condition across engine tiles, while preserving alarm-state visibility per tile.

Kardion MCS Controller work used regulated alarm behaviour under IEC 62366-1. The alarm architecture required priority tiering, visual differentiation between alarm levels, mute behaviour that kept muted alarms visible and alarm-state visibility during normal operation.

deSoutter Medical / Zethon treated the operating theatre as a demanding recognition environment. Because theatre lighting, divided attention and brief glances make colour alone unreliable, critical states were communicated through spatial position, icon form and colour.

Gexcon CFD simulation work addressed deferred fault in expert industrial software. A misconfigured simulation could appear to complete successfully and produce outputs that looked valid, so the design response made required values visible during setup and surfaced warnings for incomplete or contradictory input.

Beissbarth automotive calibration work addressed fault communication in a sequential procedure. Borderline tolerance values, measurement failures and equipment errors required distinct communication because each condition required a different corrective action.

Squaremind dermatology scanning work addressed physical process deviation by the patient. Creative Navy's Inform–Prevent–Correct framework specified what the interface must communicate when deviation occurs, how the patient is guided back to the required state and what the system must do after recovery.

The MDU ship motion monitor addressed the condition where the sensor feeding the interface stops reporting. The watchdog and no-MDU alarms were designed to communicate sensor non-reporting rather than leaving the user with an apparently current display.

bodySections.heading: Information-Availability Degradation
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Information-availability degradation is distinct from equipment fault communication. In this class, the interface must represent whether a source can be reached, whether content is cached, whether an asset is restricted, whether a record has gone stale or whether a local action has not been sent.

KISPE Space specified a common space operating picture for degradation of information availability. The central design argument was that a single global offline banner cannot describe independent lifecycles such as source outage, cached content, access restriction and local unsent action.

KISPE Space specified independent status dimensions rather than a single green-to-red health score. Designed behaviours included independent exposure of device connection, provider feed reachability and locally cached content; cached content retaining its original update time; local saved actions remaining unshared until supported confirmation; ambiguous synchronisation outcomes remaining ambiguous; concurrent edits not being silently merged; partial offline map cache showing downloaded coverage and gaps; and connection loss not clearing confirmed area.

The maritime traffic software portfolio added source degradation with a geographic consequence. The design requirement was to link the failing source to the affected layers and sector rather than reporting the failure only in a technical list. Unavailable, degraded, stale, unknown and permission-restricted were separate states rather than one collapsed condition.

bodySections.heading: Control-Channel Degradation
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Control-channel degradation concerns the path by which an instruction travels becoming unreliable while the remote system may be healthy. The interface must represent a command whose outcome is unknown without inventing certainty.

Schone Airspace Group Mission Control addressed degradation of the control channel. The leading behaviour was an elapsed response window producing an explicit unknown state that kept the target, action and request identifier and triggered no automatic retry. The reason was that an unreviewed retry of a consequential flight command is its own hazard.

Schone also separated control link condition from telemetry freshness because they fail independently. A degraded link and a stale sample are different facts with different display semantics. A value that has stopped updating keeps its last value alongside its age rather than being relabelled as current or hidden.

The handheld command-and-control engagement treated electromagnetic interference as an expected operating condition rather than as a failure exception. The engagement covered interface structure, task behaviour, information priority and clarity of operator control. The design consequences included physical commitment to signal recovery and a command-state model that treated rejection and timeout as ordinary values rather than exceptional errors.

bodySections.heading: Raymarine as an Enumeration Across Information Availability and Control-Channel Degradation
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Raymarine does not form a separate degradation class. The next-generation fixed-mount VHF sits across information-availability degradation and control-channel degradation.

Raymarine's contribution is enumeration. The engagement organised exception records against independently varying state axes: voice radio state, display context, calling transaction, AIS data quality, positioning, safety incident, interruption and chartplotter link. The governing rule was that a current screen is not a system state. The interface is a state interpreter, not the source of truth for radio outcomes.

Raymarine applied the rule that a failure is attributed to the subsystem that produced it. A lost chartplotter link is reported as a loss of chart integration rather than as a radio fault. An AIS receiver failure does not imply an empty sea. A missing registered identity is distinguished from a receiver failure. A per-feature dependency map recorded which functions survive which failure.

bodySections.heading: Outputs of the Capability
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method produces explicit abnormal-state behaviour rather than leaving fault handling to late implementation. The outputs vary by engagement, but the recurring artefacts are state models, alarm hierarchies, recovery-path definitions, dependency maps, exception catalogues, redundant-cue specifications, synchronisation rules and scenario fixtures.

For embedded and control interfaces, the capability produces visible distinctions between fault types. Sensor failure, calibration drift, stale telemetry, measurement failure, borderline tolerance and equipment non-communication do not collapse into a generic error state when they require different actions.

For command interfaces, the capability produces command-state semantics that preserve uncertainty. Requested, sending, awaiting acknowledgement, accepted, rejected, timed out and resulting state confirmed are different values when the technical system can determine them.

For information-availability interfaces, the capability produces separate status dimensions. Reachability, cached content, access permission, validity age, local unsent action and synchronisation outcome are not compressed into one health badge when that badge would make different facts look identical.

For procedural interfaces, the capability produces recovery paths embedded into the sequence. The Squaremind example used Inform–Prevent–Correct to specify what happens when a patient physically deviates from the required state, how the patient is guided back and how the guidance cycle resumes.

bodySections.heading: What this produces
bodySections.bodyMarkdown: Within Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method, this capability produces concrete interface design deliverables — interaction design, information architecture, wireframes, screen designs, interactive prototypes, and design-system components — and not advisory documents alone. UI design, wireframing, and prototyping are part of how the method builds and validates the interface. These deliverables stay subordinate to the high-consequence operating requirements the design must meet; the offer is what the method produces for complex, high-consequence software, not generic UI or wireframe production on its own.

strongClaims: Abnormal conditions, degraded modes and fault states are treated as primary design targets in this capability rather than as edge cases; this is a conceptual definition of the capability rather than an empirical outcome claim.
Kardion alarm architecture was governed by IEC 62366-1 requirements, including priority tiering, non-colour-only differentiation, mute behaviour and alarm-state visibility during normal operation.
Squaremind post-redesign ecological testing recorded 12 patient deviations in a 29-user test, and all 12 recovered in 2–4 minutes.

Schone Airspace Group degraded control-channel behaviours were evaluated against fixed scripted criteria, with first candidates recording 14 pass, 18 fail and 4 pending and the integrated retest recording 32 pass, 0 fail and 4 pending. These are design-conformance results, not operational outcome measures.

Raymarine documented 43 exception records against eight independently varying state axes. Four degraded conditions were measured in bench prototype sessions, while the remaining conditions were specified but not executed.
weakerClaims: KISPE Space documented 40 edge cases and degraded states, but its verification suites, regression checks and acceptance scenarios were written and not executed.

The handheld command-and-control engagement treated electromagnetic interference as an expected operating condition and assigned one of four physical push buttons to a signal-recovery manoeuvre. This is documented case evidence, not an outcome-measured claim.

The maritime traffic software portfolio added source degradation with a geographic consequence by linking a failing source to affected layers and sector. The validation fixtures were designed test conditions, not observations of live systems.

The MDU ship motion monitor had watchdog and no-MDU alarms for when the sensor feeding the interface stopped reporting, but the available material did not answer what the user could actually do about one screen.
limitations: KISPE Space verification suites, regression checks and acceptance scenarios were specified as executable checks but not executed.
KISPE Space scenario fixtures were designed test conditions, not data, and did not represent a real location, operation, satellite or advisory.
Schone Airspace Group pass/fail figures are design-conformance results, not task completion rates, error rates, flight measurements, airworthiness evidence or deployment evidence.
Schone Airspace Group Mission Control was built and is in test; the available material should not be described as deployment evidence.
Raymarine bench prototype sessions did not test wet hands and gloves, glare and night sailing, vibration, ambient noise or divided attention.
Raymarine's other thirty-odd degraded conditions were specified and not executed.

The handheld command-and-control engagement did not extend to autonomy, control algorithms, autonomous safety behaviour, the datalink, the effector, targeting logic, certification or weapons-review activity.
The maritime traffic software validation fixtures were designed test conditions, not observations of live radar, AIS, lock machinery or vessel traffic behaviour.
Squaremind evidence is formative; summative validation and regulatory submission are Squaremind's responsibility.
deSoutter surgeon confirmation came from structured design review sessions, not post-deployment measurement.
The MDU material documents an unanswered question about what the user can actually do about one alarm screen.

Kardion evidence records FDA approval as the process outcome and states that the alarm architecture contributed to the submitted design passing FDA evaluation; it does not isolate a specific alarm-design claim as the regulatory cause.
The products described here should not be treated as part of an AI cluster. Their unknowns are properties of links, protocols, sensors and clocks, not model uncertainty.

Design for abnormal and degraded scenarios does not create a safety, airworthiness, certification, type-approval, weapons-review or regulatory credential unless the engagement evidence explicitly states that credential.
